svg.text: 51 THIN WRAPPERS
A card reference label binds to a measure, not to a
calculation item — so each KPI gets three one-liners:
[Dead Stock Value PM] =
CALCULATE (
[Dead Stock Value],
'Time Intelligence'[Comparison] = "PM" )
17 KPIs × 3 wrappers. All logic still lives in one place;
the wrappers carry none of their own.

Badge polarity is a modelling decision, not a formatting one
The reference design tested the base measure ("spend > 0"), so its badge greened whenever spend was positive — regardless of direction.
Here the condition tests the variance, and polarity inverts for the lower-is-better half of the KPI set.
Rising is good — badge greens
Inventory Turnover · Gross Margin % · Sell-Through % · Units Sold · Gross Profit · Total Sales $
Rising is bad — badge reds (polarity inverted)
Days of Supply · Dead Stock Value · Overstock Value · Stockout SKUs · Capital at Risk · Freight % of Spend
No claim — badge stays grey
Ending Inventory Value · Total On Hand · Total Purchases $ · COGS — buying more is neither good nor bad on its own
Two guards that stop silent errors
Ratios move in percentage points
Gross Margin %, Sell-Through %, Freight % of Spend
and Days of Supply are ratios. Their variance is a
pp difference, not a percent change, so those cards
are titled "MoM Var (pp)".
Turnover is a ratio, not a percentage
[Inventory Turnover] had drifted to a percent format
string and was rendering 8.95% on the card. It is
4.20 turns per year. Restored to 0.00"x" and the
measure description now says so in capitals, so the
next person to touch it cannot repeat the mistake.
What this costs: a calculation group applies to every measure in the model, including ones it cannot help. Nine measures come from Fact_StockItem, which has no date
relationship, so the PM item has nothing to shift — those KPIs are whole-year positions and are read as single values.
Every one of the 89 measures carries a description. They are not decoration — several encode the trap that was hit while building the measure, in the place the next
person will actually read it: "Ranks over [Store Name], NOT [City]", "JANUARY 2016 ONLY", "this is a RATIO — do not let it drift back to a percent format string".
